answer: Coordination leaks through identical answer style or timing across thousands of aliases, and that fingerprint is exactly what marks them as one attacker — the more coordinated the farm, the easier it is to detect. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes.
